clue.text: One building block is hard mass but unstable

parts.note: is and but as written, with H, the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard, and m, the physics symbol for mass, between them

explanation.surface: A chemist warns that some element is heavy but liable to decay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unstable' shuffles IS, H, M and BUT; the surface nods to the element being radioactive and heavy.
explanation.definitionFit: A chemical element is one of the basic building blocks of matter, and this metal is element 83.

clue.text: I'm one in upcoming society concerned with eating disorder

indicators.note: one piece sits in the other
in a down clue, coming up means read from the bottom

explanation.walkthrough: 'upcoming' turns the society round in this down clue, and 'in' sets I'M and the numeral one inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Bulimia is an eating disorder, and the adjective describes what relates to it.

clue.text: Beatles title? Came across a greeting in one

came across means met
hi is a greeting

explanation.surface: Someone recalls encountering a hello inside a Beatles track.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one' refers back to the Beatles title, so it means a song.
explanation.definitionFit: George Harrison wrote this 1969 Beatles single, so it is an example of a Beatles title.

clue.text: Extreme state

definitions.meaning: absolute or total, as in complete nonsense

explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means total or absolute; as a verb it means to say or voice.

clue.text: Maybe Delia's book four, raw material for a vegetarian

parts.note: Delia is a woman, so what is Delia's is hers
IV is four in Roman numerals
ore is the raw material for metal

explanation.surface: Delia Smith's cookbook offers raw material for vegetarian cooking.
explanation.walkthrough: Delia Smith is a famous British cookery writer, so 'Delia's book' reads as a cookbook; here Delia just stands for any woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant eater, which is what a vegetarian is, though usually said of animals.

clue.text: Dress uniform worn inside made a hole in my pocket

parts.note: something that made a hole in my pocket cost me money

explanation.surface: A dress uniform proved expensive to buy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dress uniform' reads as one phrase, but 'Dress' is the definition and 'uniform' gives only a single letter, 'worn inside' the pocket phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A costume is a set of clothes, so as a noun it is a synonym of dress.

clue.text: What carries tee and tea

explanation.walkthrough: One word covers both the golf helper (also spelt with -ie) and the tea tin.
explanation.definitionFit: A golfer's assistant carries tees, and a tea tin stores tea, both under this one spelling.

clue.text: Criticism for wearing make-up — some find it funny

indicators.note: criticism given for wearing something follows the item worn

parts.note: slap is British slang for make-up
stick is British slang for criticism, as in taking stick

explanation.surface: Someone is mocked for wearing make-up, though others are amused.
explanation.walkthrough: SLAP (theatrical make-up) and STICK (abuse) are both British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Knockabout physical comedy is a genre many people find funny.

clue.text: 50% of wave energy is excessive

indicators.note: half of a word is kept, the rest dropped

parts.note: to undulate is to wave
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Half of a wave's energy is too much.
explanation.walkthrough: '50% of' keeps the first four of UNDULATE's eight letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Unwarranted or more than is needed is the sense, a straight synonym of excessive.

clue.text: Aged like a tree?

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether being old makes a person tree-like.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is whimsical: 'elder' is a tree, and the -ly ending makes it 'like an elder'.
explanation.definitionFit: Old in years is what aged means, and the playful reading is resembling an elder tree.

clue.text: 50mph perhaps with lights on going round M1

indicators.note: going round something encircles it, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: with the lights on a place is lit
M1 is read as the letters M and I, the one taken as the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: Driving at 50mph with headlights on around Britain's main motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is Britain's first motorway, London to Leeds; here its 1 becomes the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Fifty miles per hour is an example of a speed restriction posted on roads.

clue.text: Director and performer put in grass in middle of act

indicators.note: a thing put in another is placed within it

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass
a hand is someone who performs work, as on a farm or ship

explanation.surface: A director and actor are planted in the grass halfway through a show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in middle of act' looks like theatre staging, but it means caught in the very act.
explanation.definitionFit: Caught in the very act of wrongdoing is the idiom's sense, with blood still on the hands.

clue.text: A ground rent — it's put into my mother's property

indicators.note: a thing put into another sits inside it

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

parts.note: taken as written
it, with the 's read as 'is', a link

explanation.surface: Somebody resents ground rent being charged on their mother's house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'property' suggests real estate, but here it means a quality; 'ground' rearranges A, RENT and IT.
explanation.definitionFit: Motherhood, the state of being a parent to a child, is a quality or property belonging to a mother.

clue.text: Shout abuse as we are leaving A&E

indicators.note: letters leaving a phrase are taken out of it

parts.note: the phrase as written; that the remaining letters also run unbroken inside it is a coincidence, since the setter's instruction is to remove A and E
the hospital department's name gives the letters A and E

explanation.surface: Patients curse as they walk out of the hospital emergency unit.
explanation.walkthrough: A&E (Accident and Emergency) is the British hospital emergency department; remove the first A and last E from AS WE ARE.
explanation.definitionFit: To curse is to shout abuse, using profane language at someone.

clue.text: This little one if left for dead would be cold

indicators.note: one letter standing for another means a swap of the two

parts.note: something cold is chill

explanation.surface: A grim warning that a youngster left out would be cold.
explanation.walkthrough: Read in reverse: if L replaced D in the answer, it would become CHILL, meaning cold.
explanation.definitionFit: A kid or youngster is a little one, a common affectionate phrase.

clue.text: Cleaner put chap off

indicators.note: off completes put off, the phrase split around the chap

parts.note: put off, with chap set between, means deter
a gent is a chap

explanation.surface: A cleaning product drove a man away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put ... off' is split around 'chap', so the phrase meaning discourage comes first and the man follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Washing powder or liquid is a cleaning agent, so it is a type of cleaner.

clue.text: "I CAN'T!" Bossy heartless ridiculous pigheadedness

indicators.note: something ridiculous is absurd and out of order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped

indicators.note: a word without its heart loses its middle letter

explanation.surface: A child yells 'I can't!' at a domineering, uncaring adult.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' drops the middle S of BOSSY, leaving BOSY; 'ridiculous' shuffles that with ICANT.
explanation.definitionFit: Stubbornness, refusing to budge, is what pigheadedness means.

clue.text: A place for Sierra worth little after taking a knock?

parts.note: S is Sierra in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: one word taking another holds it inside

parts.note: cheap means worth little
a rap is a knock

explanation.surface: A cheap old Ford Sierra, after a crash, has only one place to go.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ford Sierra was a popular British family car of the 1980s; a cheap one damaged in a knock gets junked.
explanation.definitionFit: A pile of junk is the place where worthless discarded things end up.

clue.text: Certain American to cross Isle of Man cat with one that's wild

parts.note: X is a cross

indicators.note: something wild is untamed and disordered, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An American is set on crossbreeding a Manx cat with a feral one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's wild' rearranges the cat with the numeral one. The Isle of Man, between Britain and Ireland, is home to the tailless Manx cat; 'cross' is a letter shape, not breeding.
explanation.definitionFit: Self-evident and unquestionable, as an axiom is, so certain.

clue.text: Time not hanging heavy? It's a long way

definitions.meaning: a period of twelve months that is not burdensome would be a light one

explanation.surface: Someone muses that time passing lightly makes a long journey feel short.
explanation.walkthrough: Despite containing 'year', the term measures distance, not time.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the distance light travels in twelve months, nearly six trillion miles: a long way.

clue.text: When you initially went in nothing raised spirit in confinement

indicators.note: a letter that went in another word sits inside it
in a down clue, raised means read upwards

parts.note: nil is nothing

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter

parts.note: gin is a spirit

explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns NIL into LIN, and Y goes inside to make LYIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Historically the period of bed rest around childbirth, a lying-in is confinement in the old sense.

clue.text: Blade made of three metals

parts.note: K is potassium, Ni nickel and Fe iron: the chemical symbols of three metals laid side by side
K is potassium, Ni nickel and Fe iron: the chemical symbols of three metals laid side by side
K is potassium, Ni nickel and Fe iron: the chemical symbols of three metals laid side by side

explanation.surface: A blade forged from an alloy of three metals.
explanation.walkthrough: The metals are given as their chemical symbols: K, Ni, Fe.
explanation.definitionFit: A blade is a cutting tool, and the word stands for the whole implement.

clue.text: Listens for bombing and joins the army

indicators.note: bombing blows things apart, so the letters are scattered and reformed

explanation.surface: A recruit hears of the bombing and signs up.
explanation.definitionFit: Signing up for military service is what someone who enlists does.

clue.text: Unable to bear tile being missing — make a deduction

indicators.note: a word missing from another has been removed from it

parts.note: unable to bear offspring is infertile

explanation.surface: A roofer can't stand a missing tile and works out what happened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unable to bear' sounds like intolerance but means unable to have children.
explanation.definitionFit: To conclude something from evidence is to deduce it, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Was in management, invested in soccer club to get some of the old money

indicators.note: money invested in something goes inside it

parts.note: FC stands for football club
to have run something is to have managed it

explanation.surface: A former manager put old money into a football club.
explanation.definitionFit: France and other countries used this currency before the euro, so it is old money.

clue.text: Concerned with using a font that might be a bit small after cut round page?

indicators.note: what the letters might be is another arrangement of them

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: a word that is cut is trimmed short, here losing its final letter

explanation.surface: A typesetter suspects a font may be slightly too small once trimmed around the page.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' trims SMALL to SMAL; 'might be' shuffles A BIT, SMAL and P. The font is a church basin, not typography.
explanation.definitionFit: Christening takes place at a church font, so things to do with that rite involve one.

clue.text: Bung cheese round a piece of bread

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bung' is British slang for a bribe, not a stopper here.
explanation.definitionFit: Bung is British slang for an illicit payment to sway someone.

clue.text: Drive little devil to the school finally

parts.note: an imp is a little devil

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of each word

explanation.surface: A parent drives a mischievous child to school.

clue.text: Rumour of good set of exercises in the gully

explanation.definitionFit: Hearsay passed informally from person to person travels by this channel, so it stands for rumour.

clue.text: Poignancy on losing love one way and another?

O is love, a nil score in tennis

explanation.surface: Losing a lover brings poignancy, one way or another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one way and another' sounds like a shrug but literally names two routes.

clue.text: In reach but oddly elusive, knot that is maybe a bow

explanation.definitionFit: A bow tie is one kind of tie worn at the collar, so a bow is an example.

clue.text: Surrounding area locations — they're fit for a king
